question: Arun bought some pencils at the rate of ₹180 a dozen. He sold them for ₹18 each. His profit percentage is ______%.
solution:
[IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/ca81259519cadfb2d5350673c220e419e60378e9770ad26512fc8e826a8d93f1.png] __Shortcut Trick__

CP of 1 pencil = 180 ÷ 12 = ₹15

Ratio of CP : SP = 15 : 18 = 5 : 6

Profit in ratio = 6 − 5 = 1 unit on a base of 5

Profit % = (1 ÷ 5) × 100 = 20%

**∴ The correct answer is 20%.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/c76c13ba2d2ab46b47f8a931ae621dac081a0cb266b142dc23f58659fac4a466.png] **__Alternate Method__**

**Given:**

Cost Price of 1 dozen (12) pencils = ₹180

Selling Price of 1 pencil = ₹18

**Formula Used:**

Profit = SP − CP

Profit % = (Profit ÷ CP) × 100

 
 
 

 
 
 
 CP = ₹15
 
 
 SP = ₹18

 
• 
 +₹3 (Profit)

 Profit % = (3 ÷ 15) × 100 = 20%

**Calculations:**

⇒ Cost Price (CP) of 1 pencil = 180 ÷ 12 = ₹15

⇒ Selling Price (SP) of 1 pencil = ₹18

⇒ Profit = 18 − 15 = ₹3

⇒ Profit % = (3 ÷ 15) × 100

⇒ Profit % = (1 ÷ 5) × 100 = 20%

**∴ The correct answer is 20%.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **__Additional Information__**

Profit and Loss Basics

Profit occurs when the Selling Price (SP) is greater than the Cost Price (CP), calculated as Profit = SP − CP. Conversely, a loss occurs when CP > SP.

Base of Calculation

Unless otherwise explicitly mentioned in the problem, both Profit % and Loss % are always evaluated based on the initial Cost Price (CP).

Successive Discounts

When two successive discounts of a% and b% are offered, the single equivalent discount percentage is given by (a + b − ab ÷ 100)%.
